newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan financials off on state selldown plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan financials off on state selldown plan.

text.p: Taiwan's financial shares fell in early Friday trade on a government plan to sell down holdings in the island's "big three" state-run banks to alleviate the state budget deficit, brokers said.
After 55 minutes, the heavily weighted financial sector was down 1.25 percent while the broader index, itself heavily weighted toward financials, was down just 0.27 percent.
Share prices of the Big Three banks were down.
Chang Hwa fell T$2 or 1.29 percent to T$153, First Commercial was down T$2 or 1.2 percent to T$164 and Hua Nan lost T$2 or 1.57 percent to T$125.5.
A finance ministry official told Reuters by telephone that the ministry was considering selling the shares before their prices hit a selling threshold.

He said the ministry previously had planned to sell T$1.837 billion worth of First Commercial shares at T$176 per share, T$233 million worth of Huan Nan at T$188 and T$1.632 billion worth of Chang Hwa at T$184.
"The news of a state selloff is bad for overall sentiment," said United Securities' analyst Lin Long-hsien. "It makes people question the state's willingness to support the stock market."
